1  high  PHP is missing a security fix for a remote code execution flaw (ubuntu) [php.fix_missing]
   Subject       php8.3-fpm (package php8.3-fpm)
   Observed      pkg.dpkg_runtimes#1 (07:12, as deploy): php8.3-fpm 8.3.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.9 (dpkg)
   Observed      os.release#1 (07:12, as deploy): ID=ubuntu VERSION_ID=24.04
   Observed      net.listeners#1 (07:12, as deploy (sudo -n)): tcp 0.0.0.0:443 (nginx)
   Observed      fw.ufw#1 (07:12, as deploy (sudo -n)): not installed (command not found)
   Observed      fw.firewalld#1 (07:12, as deploy): not installed (command not found)
   Observed      fw.nft#1 (07:12, as deploy): empty ruleset (no tables)
   Observed      fw.iptables_backend#1 (07:12, as deploy): /usr/sbin/xtables-nft-multi
   Concluded from check:pkg.dpkg_runtimes, check:os.release, check:net.listeners, check:fw.ufw,
                  check:fw.firewalld, check:fw.nft, check:fw.iptables_backend
   Severity      high: base medium, +1 attribute serves web (net.listeners#1: tcp 0.0.0.0:443
                 (nginx))
   Why here      A web server on this host listens beyond localhost and the host firewall lets any
                 address in, which ranks one step higher. php8.3-fpm 8.3.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.9 is below
                 8.3.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.13, the first Ubuntu 24.04 package that fixes CVE-2026-109618
                 and CVE-2026-109619 (PHP security release of 21 October 2026). nginx listens on
                 0.0.0.0:443/tcp and the host firewall lets any address in, so PHP on this host is
                 reachable by whoever reaches that web server, if it passes requests to PHP. capped
                 at high: whether the cloud firewall lets anyone reach this web server, and whether
                 it passes requests to this PHP, were not read, so scheck cannot say anyone can
                 reach this PHP now.
   Not checked   Read: PHP and Node.js packages from dpkg and rpm. Not read: containers and their
                 images; Homebrew and installs from source; nvm, volta, asdf and fnm installs in
                 home directories; control-panel PHP (cPanel, Plesk, CloudLinux); Node.js inside
                 applications; other programs that bundle Brotli; whether running processes were
                 restarted after an update. Advisories published after 2026-10-24, the date of this
                 build's table, are not known to it; Filters outside nftables (eBPF programs such as
                 Cilium's) were not read
   Fix           Update PHP from the source you installed it from, then restart every PHP process:
                 an installed update does not protect workers that were started before it.
                 Caveat: Until you can update: set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and
                   post_max_size=8M (32M if you accept uploads) in php.ini or the FPM pool, not in
                   .user.ini. These reduce the risk; they do not remove it.
                 Commands (review before running):
                   sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade   # Debian, Ubuntu
                   sudo dnf upgrade 'php*'   # Red Hat family, Fedora
                   sudo systemctl restart php8.3-fpm   # and Apache or the web server, if PHP runs inside it
